clearing_status.fact: As of October 4 2026 (tokenpost.com), the Dec 31 2026 (cash) and Jun 30 2027 (repo) deadlines remain operative under the single one-year extension published as 90 FR 11134 (Feb 25 2025). SEC Commissioner Uyeda stated at the Sept 22 2026 U.S. Treasury Market Conference that the agency 'does not currently intend to extend these deadlines.' No second extension has been announced.
clearing_status.rationale: The rubric scores 1 for an official extension already granted; 90 FR 11134 is that extension and remains the sole operative delay. No second extension or passed-deadline event has occurred, so rubric level 2 is not triggered.

plan_financing.fact: 10y JGB yield eased to ~2.78% on Oct 26 (TradingEconomics), down ~34bps from the ~3.12% peak; 20-year JGB auction Oct 20 hit a record bid-to-cover of 5.84x (prev 4.01x, 12-mo avg 3.73x) — Bloomberg/MOF Oct 20 2026. Takaichi on Oct 19 reiterated 'no preset idea on extra budget' and plan to maintain issuance at 'appropriate level' (FXStreet Oct 19 2026), still without specifying a concrete supplementary budget funding mechanism.
plan_financing.rationale: Auctions are clearing firmly well above the rubric's >3 BTC threshold (record 5.84x for 20y) and the 10y yield is falling, not rising >25bps on fiscal news — ruling out a score of 2. However, the funding path for the next fiscal package remains unspecified (verbal 'restraint' pledges only, no concrete supplementary budget with full debt issuance detail), keeping the indicator at 1 per the rubric's 'funding path unspecified' criterion.
plan_financing.change_reason: new_event: 20-year JGB auction Oct 20 2026 produced a record bid-to-cover of 5.84x and 10y yield continued falling to 2.78% by Oct 26, materially improving auction/yield optics post-Oct 19, but value unchanged at 1 as fiscal funding path for the next round of stimulus remains unspecified

dissent.view: centralbank.watch (Oct 23) shows 10y yield at 3.06% in its term structure table, somewhat higher than TradingEconomics 2.78% — possible data lag or OTC vs. futures pricing difference

direct_lending_default.fact: Fitch Ratings recorded a U.S. Private Credit Default Rate (PCDR) of 6.3% for the trailing 12 months ended August 2026, up from 6.1% in July 2026, a record high across ~1,300 borrowers inclusive of distressed exchanges, PIK conversions, maturity extensions, and other liability-management exercises; 89 unique defaulters generated 109 default events in the TTM period. Source: Fitch Ratings report published September 15, 2026, as reported by The Lead PC (theleadpc.com/middle-market-private-credit-9-14-2026/), Bloomberg (bloomberg.com, September 14 2026), and Investment Executive (investmentexecutive.com, September 14 2026).
direct_lending_default.rationale: The Fitch PCDR of 6.3% (TTM Aug-2026, published Sep-15-2026) is the most recent available Fitch print under the rubric's anchor methodology; no newer Fitch PCDR publication for September or October 2026 was found, so the prior reading is retained unchanged per rubric. The rate sits at a series record and has held at or above 6.0% since April 2026, with the August spike driven by 14 monthly default events (highest in the trailing year), corroborated by a concurrent Fed rate hike to 3.75-4.00% on Sep-16-2026 that further pressures floating-rate borrowers.

dissent.view: Proskauer Private Credit Default Index: 2.51% for Q2 2026 (counts payment and financial-covenant defaults only, excludes maturity extensions); down from 2.73% in Q1 2026 across 716 loans / $195.6B principal
KBRA Middle Market Default Monitor: 3.3% by count and 2.4% by debt for TTM to June 30 2026 (adds imminent defaults and interventions but excludes pure maturity extensions)

Moody's private credit estimate: 1.6%-4.7% range for full-year 2025, depending on whether distressed exchanges are counted; October 2026 Moody's note cites 'true rate 5.8% vs. reported 4%' masked by PIK use
UBS 2026 forecast: projects private credit defaults could reach 9%-10% by end of 2026 under stress scenario

redemption_gates.fact: Fitch Ratings data reported Oct 13 2026 (Blue Vault Oct 15 2026): nontraded BDC redemption requests averaged 9.8% across 13 of 15 perpetual-life funds in Q3 2026 — nearly twice the 5% quarterly cap. Named funds prorating at 5% in Q3: BCRED (~$79B, ~10% requests, third straight quarter of proration per Sept 3 SEC letter); HLEND (~$25B, ~11.5% requests, second consecutive prorated quarter); CCLFX (Cliffwater, ~16% requests, above cap). S&P downgraded BCRED outlook to stable from positive in Oct 2026 citing NAV declines. Combined AUM of gated funds far exceeds $100B.
redemption_gates.rationale: Three named funds — BCRED, HLEND, CCLFX — are actively prorating redemptions at the 5% quarterly cap in Q3 2026 with combined AUM well above $100B, satisfying the rubric threshold of >=3 of the largest funds or combined AUM >$100B for a score of 2 (WIDESPREAD). No corroborating rate or spread signals contradict this structural gating stress (Fitch default rate at 6.1% record high in July 2026 and S&P BCRED outlook downgrade in Oct 2026 are consistent).

dissent.view: Some Q3 data (angelinvestorsnetwork Sep 11 read) suggests BDEBT cleared its 5% cap without proration and HLEND/CCLFX requests declined from Q2, implying marginal improvement in breadth — but BCRED, HLEND, and CCLFX are still gating above cap in Q3, so rubric outcome unchanged

new_imf_programs.fact: Within Apr 26–Oct 26 2026, the IMF Executive Board approved three distinct new nonprecautionary lending arrangements: (1) Rwanda ECF ~Jun 8 2026 (IMF PR 26/191); (2) Mauritania ECF+EFF ~Jun 27 2026 (Panapress/IMF); (3) Bolivia EFF Oct 2 2026 (IMF Executive Board, confirmed by Bloomberg, Bretton Woods Project, report.az, CGTN). new_imf_programs.rationale: Three distinct sovereigns (Rwanda, Mauritania, Bolivia) each had a brand-new nonprecautionary IMF lending arrangement approved by the Executive Board within the trailing 6-month window; rubric specifies CLUSTER (value=2) for 3 or more countries. No sovereign defaults or distressed exchanges add to the count. [vintage guard: new read is 2026-10-02 data but the prior applied value was 2026-10-12 data; kept the newer vintage]

china_ppi.fact: China PPI rose +5.0% year-on-year in September 2026, per NBS data released 14 October 2026; corroborated by investing.com (actual 5.0%, forecast 4.4%, previous 3.8%), tradingeconomics.com, CNBC, and Caixin Global. Next NBS release (Oct 2026 PPI) is scheduled 9 November 2026 — not yet published as of 26 October 2026.
china_ppi.rationale: The rubric requires the signed NBS-published YoY figure; +5.0% for September 2026 is confirmed by multiple primary-corroborating sources with no material disagreement. No newer data exists, so the prior reading stands unchanged.

trade_actions.fact: As of Oct 26, 2026, the US Section 301 forced-labor tariff of 12.5% on all Chinese goods (91 FR 47318, effective July 24, 2026) remains in force with no injunction (htsbase.com, Oct 22, 2026). Post-Oct-17 additions include: EU maintained definitive AD on preserved citrus fruits from China (EU 2026/2327, Oct 22, 2026, eulawlive.com); EU sunset review initiated on Chinese aluminium flat-rolled products (14.3%-24.6%) on Oct 9, 2026 (metal.com); China launched AD probe into p-nitrotoluene, early Oct 2026 (Euronews Oct 3); EU-China 'shared understanding' on hybrid vehicle export curbs reached Oct 8-9 (brusselstimes.com). One partial offset: EU repealed AD/CVD on Chinese solar glass Oct 21-22 (metal.com). Total confirmed major-economy measures in trailing 3 months remains well above 4, anchored by the July 24 US broad 12.5% tariff covering all Chinese goods.
trade_actions.rationale: The rubric requires level 2 (ESCALATING) for >=4 new measures OR a broad tariff round >=10% across a sector. The US July 24 12.5% forced-labor tariff alone covers all Chinese goods (a broad round >=10%), and the total count of confirmed new measures in the trailing 3 months exceeds 7. Nothing post-Oct-17 changes the rubric outcome; the prior reading correctly applied the rubric.

dissent.view: US-China trade truce extended to Jan 10, 2027 (late-September 2026 Bessent statement) and US-China listed $30bn in goods for possible future tariff cuts (Sept 27 Xi Washington visit), suggesting a managed détente rather than open escalation; however the 12.5% tariff and multiple EU AD duties remain in force, so the rubric threshold is still met.

license_flow.fact: MOFCOM Announcement No. 18 (April 4, 2025) — imposing case-by-case export licensing on seven medium/heavy rare earths (Sm, Gd, Tb, Dy, Lu, Sc, Y) and derivative magnets including NdFeB and SmCo — remains fully in force and unpaused as of mid-October 2026. Processing times run 45 days to several months (rare-earth-mining.com, accessed Oct 2026). General licences issued from December 2025 to named large producers (JL Mag, Yunsheng, Zhong Ke San Huan) for pre-cleared civilian end-users supplement but do not replace the case-by-case regime (technology.org, 19 Oct 2026; rare-earth-mining.com). The broader October 2025 controls (Announcements 55-58, 61, 62) remain suspended until at least 10 November 2026 under MOFCOM Announcement No. 70; a MOFCOM official statement of 28 September 2026 indicated the underlying arrangement extends to 10 January 2027, but no formal published MOFCOM announcement confirms this extension as of 11 October 2026 (mainrichinternational.com, 11 Oct 2026; rare-earth-mining.com, 11 Oct 2026).
license_flow.rationale: The rubric scores 1 ('SLOWING') when approvals are limited to named producers/end-users OR typical processing exceeds 30 days. Both conditions are met: general licences are confined to whitelisted Chinese producers with pre-vetted civilian customers, all other exports require individual case-by-case MOFCOM review with documented processing times of 45 days to several months. No categorical suspension of all licensing (score 2) and no blanket open regime (score 0) applies.

dissent.view: BISI (late September 2026) states the October 2025 suspension has been extended to 10 January 2027 following a Trump-Xi Washington summit, implying the broader control package remains paused beyond November 10; however, no formal MOFCOM announcement confirming this extension was published as of 11 October 2026 per rareearthdirectory.com and mainrichinternational.com, making it an unconfirmed verbal statement rather than an official notice.

informedclearly.com characterises EU approval rates as 'below 25%' and describes 'sixfold price spikes' suggesting conditions closer to rubric level 2; however, these claims are unverified by MOFCOM data or Reuters commodity pricing and appear to conflate the suspended October measures with the still-active April regime.

truce_status.fact: Truce extended to Jan 10, 2027 per Bessent (Sep 23 2026) and MOFCOM official statement (Sep 28 2026); no further renewal announced. Jan 10 2027 is 76 days from today, inside the 90-day rubric window. MOFCOM's legal text (Announcement No. 70, 2025) still reads 'until 10 November 2026' with no published formal notice changing that date as of Oct 16-19 2026 (technology.org / mainrichinternational.com, Oct 2026). China's compliance assessed at ~two-thirds of committed rare earth shipment volumes (Cryptobriefing/preparatory talks report, Sep 2026).
truce_status.rationale: Jan 10 2027 is 76 days from Oct 26 2026, placing the truce squarely inside the 90-day expiry window with no renewal announced — the rubric's core EXPIRING condition is met. US officials have also cited materially below-committed shipment volumes, a secondary fraying signal under the rubric.

dissent.view: MOFCOM's formal legal text (Announcement No. 70, 2025) still lists Nov 10 2026 as the expiry with no published amendment as of Oct 16-19; the Jan 10 2027 date rests only on oral/political statements, meaning some compliance teams treat Nov 10 as the operative legal deadline rather than Jan 10.

re_blacklist.fact: MOFCOM Announcement No. 23 of 2026 (22 June 2026) placed MP Materials Corp. and USA Rare Earth, Inc. on China's Export Control List, prohibiting supply of China-origin dual-use items to those two named firms. As of 16 October 2026, the listing remains 'In force' with no removal or delisting detected (aihorizonnetwork.com timeline, dated 16 Oct 2026). Benchmark Minerals explicitly characterises the measure as 'entity-specific rather than a blanket restriction on rare earth exports to the US.'
re_blacklist.rationale: Two named US rare-earth producers are listed under a firm-specific designation (rubric value 1); the restriction has not been broadened to a categorical sector-wide ban covering all US rare-earth producers as a class (which would be rubric value 2). No removal or delisting has been confirmed, so value 0 does not apply.

hree_premium.fact: CREIA reported dysprosium oxide at $209-215/kg inside China on Oct 26, 2026; REEx (Oct 26) estimates ex-China dysprosium oxide at $2,500-5,500/kg (midpoint ~$4,000/kg, ~19x), while S&P Global's most recent formal assessment (September 2026) placed North American dysprosium at $3,250/kg (~15-16x). Source: Rare Earth Exchanges (rareearthexchanges.com, Oct 26 2026); S&P Global via REEx (Oct 26 2026).
hree_premium.rationale: The S&P Global formal assessment of $3,250/kg ex-China against $212/kg China domestic remains the most anchored price-discovery benchmark at ~15x, consistent with the prior reading; REEx's Oct 26 estimate range of $2,500-5,500/kg suggests the ceiling has widened but does not displace the formal benchmark multiple.

dissent.view: REEx Oct 26 2026 estimates ex-China dysprosium at $2,500-5,500/kg vs $209-215/kg China domestic, implying a midpoint multiple of ~19x and a ceiling of ~26x, materially above the 15x anchor
REEx Oct 17 2026 reports ex-China dysprosium up to $5,500/kg vs ~$200/kg China (~27x ceiling), citing unauthorized export opacity inflating spread

genius_impl.fact: OCC issued its GENIUS Act final rule on October 21, 2026 (OCC News Release 2026-92; OCC Bulletin 2026-50), effective January 18, 2027 — becoming the first primary federal regulator to finalize. The Federal Reserve remains at the NPRM stage (two NPRMs issued September 24, 2026, comment period open until November 30, 2026); FDIC and NCUA have not finalized. The Section 13 statutory deadline of July 18, 2026 was missed by all agencies; OCC finalized ~3 months late with BSA/AML/OFAC rules deferred to a separate Treasury rulemaking.
genius_impl.rationale: The OCC final rule (October 21, 2026) removes the 'no final rules at all' condition that drove the prior score-2 reading, but the Federal Reserve, FDIC, and NCUA remain in proposed/comment stage — documented inter-agency divergence fitting the rubric's score-1 condition of 'rules still in proposed/comment stage near the deadline, OR documented inter-agency divergence.' Score 2 is no longer warranted because at least one binding final rule now exists.
genius_impl.change_reason: new_event: OCC issued GENIUS Act final rule on 2026-10-21 (OCC News Release 2026-92), the first primary federal regulator to finalize; prior score-2 was predicated on zero final rules, which no longer holds.

ai_revenue_gap.fact: Microsoft FY26 Q4 (ended Jun 30, reported Jul 29, 2026; SEC 8-K / microsoft.com/investor): capex $41B +70% YoY; Azure +43% YoY (accelerating from Q3's 40%); Azure crossed $100B annual revenue; Q1 FY27 capex guided >$50B with Azure ~45% guided. ai_revenue_gap.change_reason: new_event: Microsoft FY26 Q4 reported Jul 29 2026 updated capex to $41B (+70% YoY) and Azure to +43% YoY (accelerating); combined hyperscaler 2026 capex guidance revised to ~$730B; prior reading was based on Apr 29 Q3 data only.

regional_bank_stress.fact: FDIC failed-bank list (fdic.gov, confirmed Oct 26 2026) shows no new failures after Sep 25 2026; the trailing 6-month window (Apr 26 – Oct 26 2026) contains 5 failures: Community Bank and Trust-West Georgia (May 1), Kentland Federal S&L (Jul 10), Small Business Bank (Jul 17), Tioga-Franklin Savings Bank (Aug 21), and Nano Banc (Sep 25, $736M assets). No new post-Sep-25 failures or enforcement actions alter the prior reading. [cross-check (asi1): two reads disagreed (1 vs 0); held for review]

dollar_reserve_share.fact: IMF COFER data brief published 30 September 2026 (data.imf.org / centralbanking.com): the dollar's share of allocated global foreign exchange reserves was 56.70% at end-June 2026, down from 57.13% in Q1 2026. Source: https://www.centralbanking.com/central-banks/economics/data/7977210/dollars-share-of-foreign-reserves-fell-slightly-in-q2-imf
dollar_reserve_share.rationale: The rubric asks for the latest USD share of allocated global FX reserves as a percent; the IMF COFER Q2 2026 release (30 Sep 2026) reports exactly 56.70%, confirmed by multiple sources including coferdata.com and maseconomics.com. No Q3 2026 COFER release exists yet (next expected December 2026), so 56.7 remains the current authoritative reading.

weaponization_event.fact: As of the Oct 15-16 EU summit, the EU has not seized Russian sovereign reserves; the status remains a freeze (extended to Sep 2029 on Sep 22, 2026) plus a collateralized loan architecture. The New Delhi BRICS Declaration (Sep 12-13) formally endorsed BRICS Pay local-currency interoperability, but Epoch Times analysis (citing AP, Sep 2026) states BRICS Pay 'is not operational' and 'remains a proposal and development project.' No new sovereign reserve seizure or major-economy operational reserve settlement shift off USD occurred after Oct 19, 2026.
weaponization_event.rationale: The Russian asset freeze remains an immobilization/freeze, not a confiscation or legal title transfer, so rubric Level 2 is not triggered. BRICS Pay endorsement at New Delhi constitutes new non-dollar settlement agreement/launch rhetoric but not an operational clearing mechanism, sustaining Level 1.

dissent.view: Several non-primary sources (informedclearly.com, economy.com.pk) claim BRICS Pay 'went live' or began 'operational deployment' in 2026, which if true would push closer to Level 2 territory for settlement shift; however these sources conflict with AP-cited Epoch Times analysis from the summit itself confirming non-operational status.

insurer_exits.fact: NAIC August 2026 report (715 carriers, 2018-2024) confirmed company-initiated non-renewal rates rose 96%-216% across all four U.S. regions; Foster (2026) documents elevated non-renewal rates in 13 states; Weiss Ratings Sep 8 2026 named Utah new epicenter at 4.45% non-renewal rate. No top-10 homeowners insurer fully exited a major state post-Sep 8: Travelers committed to CA expansion (Apr 2026), Allstate refiled to re-enter CA new business (Sep 1 2026), State Farm rate settlement final Jul 23 2026 with no-new-block-nonrenewal pledge through 2026. Sources: NAIC 'Examining Homeowner Property Insurance Market Dynamics' (Aug 5 2026); AdvoraHQ full insurer exit list (updated Oct 2026); financedevil.com NAIC data compilation (Oct 7 2026).
insurer_exits.rationale: Non-renewal waves are confirmed elevated across 13 states, fitting the rubric's 5-15 state band for value=1 (RISING). No new top-10 insurer fully exited a major state after Sep 8 2026 — the threshold for value=2 — and several top-10 carriers are actively re-entering CA, indicating partial stabilization rather than acceleration.

cat_losses.fact: Gallagher Re Q3 2026 Natural Catastrophe and Climate Report (Oct 21 2026): global insured cat losses USD 92bn for 9M 2026, 29% below the 10-yr average of USD 128bn, lowest 9-month total since 2019; six consecutive quarters without a single event >USD 10bn in insured losses. Hurricane Isaias (Cat 2, Oct 9) excluded from 9M total; Gallagher Re expects low-to-mid single-digit USD bn in insured losses from Isaias.
cat_losses.rationale: YTD insured losses of USD 92bn are 72% of the USD 128bn 10-year average, well below the 100% threshold for ELEVATED and far below 150% for SEVERE; no single event has exceeded USD 10bn, satisfying both conditions for NORMAL (0). Adding Isaias at USD 2-4bn best estimate keeps YTD ~74% of average and still below the single-event USD 10bn threshold.

ss_reform_news.fact: 2026 SSA Trustees Report (June 9, 2026, ssa.gov/oact/) projects OASI depletion Q4 2032 (one quarter earlier than 2025) and combined OASDI depletion 2034; 75-year actuarial deficit widened to 4.42% of payroll. H.R.9187 (Bipartisan Social Security Commission Act) referred to House Ways and Means Committee on 06/08/2026 with no further floor action (congress.gov, latest action 06/08/2026). PROMISE Act introduced Senate July 2026, not passed. Only SSA bills signed post-09/28/2026: H.R.5345 (Identity Theft Act, Oct 7) and Social Security Claiming Age Clarity Act (passed Senate Sept 30, awaiting signature) -- neither alters benefits or trust-fund solvency. No automatic cut has been triggered; current benefits unchanged.
ss_reform_news.rationale: The trustees report worsened the depletion date and reform legislation is actively debated in both chambers, satisfying rubric band 1 (DEBATE). No bill enacting benefit cuts or solvency reform has been enacted, and the automatic cut trigger (trust fund depletion) remains ~6 years away, so band 2 (CUTS) is not met.

pension_leverage_event.fact: Spence & Partners (Oct 22 2026, spenceandpartners.co.uk): 'in the recent UK gilt market volatility, it\'s been relatively smooth sailing in comparison to the events of four years ago,' corroborated by IFS (Oct ~9 2026, ifs.org.uk): \'2026 is not a rerun of 2022\' and by AlphaSquawk (Aug 2026): March 2026 gilt selloff produced only \'limited pension cash calls\' described as \'far smaller than in 2022,\' with lower leverage and improved collateral; BoE FPC April 2026 record confirms LDI sector remained resilient with 250 bps buffer standard in force.
pension_leverage_event.rationale: All post-Oct-12 sources confirm LDI buffers are adequate and no margin-call episode or forced gilt selling has occurred; rubric condition for score 1 or 2 (regulator flag of stress, or forced selling/CB intervention) is not met. Score 0 (NONE) is correct.

funded_ratio.fact: Milliman 100 Public Pension Funding Index (PPFI) funded ratio: 88.2% as of July 31, 2026, covering the 100 largest U.S. public defined benefit plans. Source: Milliman PPFI August 2026 update (published August 27, 2026), https://www.milliman.com/en/insight/public-pension-funding-index-august-2026 and https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260827829119/en/Milliman-analysis-Public-pension-funded-ratio-slips-again-to-88.2-as-of-July-31
funded_ratio.rationale: The PPFI funded ratio of 88.2% as of July 31, 2026 maps directly to the rubric, which calls for a representative large U.S. public-pension funded ratio as a percent. No subsequent PPFI monthly update (August or September 2026 public pension data) has been published as of October 26, 2026; the October 2026 Milliman PFI release (114.5%) covers corporate plans, not public plans, and is a different index.

interconnection_months.fact: LBNL Queued Up: 2026 Edition (data workbook May 2026, PDF June 2026, emp.lbl.gov/queues): 'The median project built in 2025 took 61 months from the interconnection request to commercial operations' — down from 63 months for the 2024 in-service cohort.
interconnection_months.rationale: The primary LBNL source directly reports 61 months as the median IR-to-COD for the 2025 in-service cohort, confirmed by both the official PDF and multiple secondary aggregators; this maps mechanically to a reading of 61. No newer LBNL edition has been published after June 2026, so the value is unchanged.

dc_moratoria.fact: electricchoice.com (updated Oct 15, 2026) tracks '575 active restrictions across 46 states'; NY Gov. Hochul signed EO 62 on Jul 14, 2026 — the first confirmed statewide moratorium — still in force; 11 additional governors (TX, PA, VA, MA, KY, OH, OR, UT, NE, NV, LA) have issued restricting executive orders/directives (electricchoice.com); hundreds of enacted local/county moratoria confirmed in NJ (93), OH (55), GA (52), NC (52), CA (29), CO (23), FL (32), WI (45), WA (19) and others; post-Oct-16 additions include Grant County NM (Oct 22) and San Diego Mayor-signed moratorium (Oct 23).
dc_moratoria.rationale: The rubric's level-2 threshold requires a confirmed statewide moratorium OR >10 jurisdictions with enacted pauses — both conditions are exceeded many times over: one confirmed statewide EO (NY), 11 additional governor-level directives, and 575 local/state enacted restrictions across 46 states. No new post-Oct-16 event changes the rubric outcome; the reading correctly held at 2.

dissent.view: ailawsbystate.com (Oct 8, 2026) states 'no state legislature has enacted a statewide data center moratorium,' distinguishing executive orders from legislative enactment; on this narrow statutory reading, only EOs are in force at the state level.

ai_power_pressure.fact: DOE Order No. 202-26-50 (issued Oct 12, 2026; effective Oct 13-16, 2026) authorized PJM to direct data-center backup generators as a last resort before/during an EEA-3 event, citing 111,500 MW forecast demand, 61,591 MW of generation outages, and a reserve margin within 900 MW - a second confirmed Section 202(c) emergency grid-reliability order targeting data-center load since the July 1-3, 2026 orders. Source: DOE (energy.gov/documents/doe-order-no-202-26-50) and PJM application Oct 11, 2026.
ai_power_pressure.rationale: A formally issued DOE 202(c) order specifically authorizing curtailment of data-center grid load meets the rubric's top band ('confirmed curtailment of data-center load' or 'declared grid emergency'); this is the second such order in 2026 within 13 weeks, with a third (Oct 13-16) now confirmed post the Oct 9 reading date. The 6,831 MW PJM capacity shortfall and ~8-year interconnection queue remain structurally unresolved, sustaining the ACUTE classification.
ai_power_pressure.change_reason: new_event: DOE Order No. 202-26-50 (Oct 12-16, 2026) issued a third Section 202(c) emergency authorization for PJM data-center backup-generator curtailment authority, occurring after the Oct 9 last-reading date and confirming ACUTE conditions are ongoing rather than historical

dissent.view: DOE order authorizes curtailment as a 'last resort' and one source notes no public record confirms backup generators were actually activated during Oct 13-16 period, which could argue for rating 1 (tight but no forced curtailment)

mine_disruptions.fact: Grasberg Block Cave (world #2 copper mine) reached only 67% of normal milling capacity as of October 2, 2026 (Northern Miner, Oct 2 2026), still ramping from the Sep 2025 mud rush; Q1 2026 produced only 95 Mlb vs ~425 Mlb normal quarterly rate (Freeport 8-K). Full restart now delayed to early 2028. Kamoa-Kakula 2026 guidance tightened to 290,000-310,000t (Ivanhoe Q2 results, Jul 29 2026), down from original 380,000-420,000t, following 2025 seismic/flooding; H1 2026 output only ~135,700t. S&P Global (Oct 2026, LME Week) confirms top-20 mine output fell 2.5% YoY in H1 2026; Sprott/KuCoin confirm combined Grasberg+Kamoa outages erased ~600,000t of expected 2026 output, with institutions (Goldman Sachs, Benchmark Mineral Intelligence) forecasting a copper market deficit.
mine_disruptions.rationale: At least two top-20 mines (Grasberg #2, Kamoa-Kakula top-5) have confirmed active, material production cuts ongoing into Q4 2026, with combined lost output (~600,000t) large enough that multiple major institutions explicitly forecast a 2026 copper market deficit - satisfying the rubric's CLUSTER condition of >=3 major mines OR lost output sufficient for institutional deficit forecasts.

dissent.view: Grasberg ramp-up is progressing - BMO analyst Katja Jancic called the restart 'progressing well' as of Oct 2, and Freeport targets 65% capacity in H2 2026, suggesting partial recovery rather than full outage

copper_deficit_timing.fact: ICSG October 2026 biannual forecast (issued 14-15 Oct 2026): global refined copper market surplus of ~104,000 metric tons in 2026, widening to ~368,000 mt in 2027; corroborated by ICSG monthly bulletin (Oct 23, 2026) showing Jan-Aug 2026 cumulative refined surplus of 218,000 mt. Sources: Mining Weekly (15 Oct 2026), Northern Miner (16 Oct 2026), ICSG monthly bulletin via SMM/theindustryspread (23 Oct 2026).
copper_deficit_timing.rationale: ICSG forecasts a 2026 refined copper surplus of ~104,000 mt, which is unambiguously above zero and above the +/-100kt balanced band, mapping directly to rubric band 0 (SURPLUS). The Jan-Aug 2026 actual cumulative surplus of 218,000 mt physically corroborates the full-year surplus forecast.

drought_chip_farm.fact: Taiwan: WRA data via reservoirs.earth (Oct 22 2026) shows 22 tracked reservoirs at 59.2% combined capacity, 'within their normal operating range,' 0 of 22 in severely dry or worse drought conditions, no rationing order in force (March 2026 order expired ~July 2026). US Southwest: U.S. Drought Monitor (droughtmonitor.unl.edu, data valid Oct 20, released Oct 22 2026) reports drought improved across the West with no deterioration; significant drought persists in the Great Basin and parts of California/Nevada (long-term D3-D4 in AZ per azwater.gov Sep 2026 quarterly), but no fab or farm water-rationing/curtailment order confirmed in force or imposed within the last 90 days.
drought_chip_farm.rationale: Taiwan reservoirs are at normal operating levels (~59%) with no active rationing order, disqualifying Level 2. The US Southwest retains persistent severe-to-extreme drought in the Great Basin and California long-term, meeting Level 1 (D2 severe persists, D3 present in some areas), but no confirmed production curtailment or rationing order at a chip fab or major farm hub is in force or was imposed within the last 90 days, so Level 2 is not supported.
drought_chip_farm.change_reason: correction: The prior safeguard held Level 2 despite the March 2026 Taiwan rationing order having expired ~July 2026 (>90 days before today) and Taiwan reservoirs recovering to ~59-61% (normal range per WRA/reservoirs.earth Oct 22 2026). No US Southwest fab/farm curtailment order is confirmed within the 90-day window. The rubric correctly maps to Level 1.

dissent.view: Arizona azwater.gov (Sep 2026 quarterly) confirms D3-D4 Exceptional/Extreme long-term drought in every county; Lake Powell ~22% capacity (Oct 20) - these could support Level 2 if a curtailment order exists, but none is confirmed in sources.

reservoir_stress.fact: Lake Mead elevation 1,037.9 ft, storage 6,831,103 acre-feet, 24% of USBR active capacity (26,120,000 AF basis) as of Oct 25, 2026 — a new all-time record low since first filling; minimum power pool is 950 ft, reservoir ~88 ft above that threshold. Source: USBR gauge data via lakelevelnow.com (Oct 25 2026); corroborated by USBR Weekly Hydrologic Update (Oct 18 2026): 1,037.24 ft, 26%.
reservoir_stress.rationale: At 24-26% of active capacity, Lake Mead is well below the rubric's 30% CRITICAL threshold (<30%), satisfying the top-band criterion; the reservoir also sits ~88 ft above the 950 ft minimum power pool, which is within the 15-ft sub-criterion only if it were <15 ft away (it is not), but the <30% storage criterion alone is sufficient for a score of 2.

dissent.view: lakelevelstoday.com reports 42.6% of pool on Oct 23 2026 — this appears to use full pool capacity (1,229 ft / ~28.23 maf) as denominator rather than USBR active storage capacity (26,120,000 AF), yielding a higher percentage; USBR active-capacity basis gives 26%.

water_dispute.fact: Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif, at a joint press event in Islamabad on 21 October 2026, publicly declared that any violation of the Indus Waters Treaty by India 'will be regarded by Pakistan as an act of war,' describing water as a national red line (Pakistan Today, Daily Times, Emra News, 21 Oct 2026). India's IWT abeyance remains in force.
water_dispute.rationale: The rubric's Level 2 threshold is met: within the last 90 days, a head of government (Pakistan's PM) issued an explicit, on-the-record war threat tied directly to a river treaty. This is a new qualifying event after the prior reading date of 2026-10-15, upgrading from 1 to 2.
water_dispute.change_reason: new_event: Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif issued an explicit 'act of war' threat tied to the Indus Waters Treaty at a public press event in Islamabad on 21 October 2026 — after the prior reading date of 2026-10-15 — satisfying the Level 2 head-of-state war threat criterion.

fao_food_trend.fact: FAO Food Price Index averaged 136.0 points in September 2026, up 2.0 points (+1.5%) MoM from revised August and +5.8% YoY; third consecutive monthly increase and highest since November 2022. Source: FAO (fao.org/worldfoodsituation/foodpricesindex), released 2 October 2026.
fao_food_trend.rationale: MoM gain of 1.5% is above zero (ruling out band 0) but below the 3% threshold required for band 2, and the 3-month cumulative rise does not reach 10%; index is at a multi-year high and rising, fitting band 1 (ELEVATED) precisely. No newer monthly release exists as of 26 October 2026 (next due 6 November).

china_export_curbs.fact: Per Argus Media data cited by global-agriculture.com (Oct 19 2026) and UkrAgroConsult (Oct 15 2026): China phosphate fertilizer exports have fallen from 5.3 mln tonnes in 2025 to 'almost nothing' in 2026, with the NDRC-initiated suspension (Dec 2025, extended per Fertilizer Daily Jul 29 2026 'at least through August 2026') still de-facto operative post-August with no confirmed resumption. Urea exports continue under controlled quota/price-floor arrangements (3.3 Mt cap cited by GIDEX Sep 18 2026, with FOB floors of $430-440/t), unchanged from prior reading.
china_export_curbs.rationale: Both phosphate suspension and urea quota remain in force with no authoritative confirmation of lifting; the phosphate near-zero export reality post-August confirms the restriction persists. No NEW product added or quota lowered in the trailing 3 months from Oct 26 2026, so rubric band 2 is not triggered; band 1 (IN PLACE, unchanged) applies.

dissent.view: Fertiaxis.com (Oct 24 2026) argues the widely-cited '3.3 Mt urea quota' is actually an import tariff-rate quota for urea entering China, not an export ceiling - meaning the urea export restriction mechanism differs from how it has been characterised by GIDEX/DiscoveryAl; separately, UkrAgroConsult/Argus (Oct 15 2026) forecast full-year 2026 urea exports at 6-7 Mt, well above 3.3 Mt, consistent with fertiaxis's reading.

hormuz_fertilizer.fact: IMF PortWatch recorded 4 commercial transits through the Strait of Hormuz on October 18, 2026, against a pre-crisis baseline of ~85 per day — 5% of baseline. Source: straits.live (sourcing portwatch.imf.org feed), October 26 daily brief; corroborated by straits.live/today (verified 4 days ago).
hormuz_fertilizer.rationale: 4 transits against an 85/day baseline equals ~5% of normal, well below the 25% threshold required for a CUT (value=2) rating; Gulf fertilizer, sulfur and ammonia loadings through Hormuz are implicitly near-zero given the strait has been effectively closed for 236 days, confirming the CUT classification.

dissent.view: Wikipedia/Kpler (as of Oct 21) estimates oil flows through Hormuz including offshore transfers in the Gulf of Oman at ~14 million bbl/day or ~82% of pre-war levels — but this covers pipeline and offshore transfer workarounds, not commercial vessel transits through the strait itself, and does not contradict the PortWatch vessel count.
thehormuzstrait.com (Windward data, Oct 7) logged 18 transits on Oct 7 (~20% of 88/day baseline), higher than PortWatch's count but still below the 25% threshold for CUT.

taiwan_tension.fact: Taiwan MND bulletin (X post, 26 Oct 2026, covering to 0600 UTC+8 26 Oct): 3 sorties of PLA aircraft, 6 PLAN vessels and 9 official ships detected around Taiwan; 1 of 3 sorties crossed the median line into Taiwan's southwestern and eastern ADIZ. ROC Armed Forces monitored and responded. Context: Oct 12-17 PLA live-fire drills in 5 coastal zones (Bohai, Yellow Sea, East China Sea, South China Sea) were assessed by Taiwan MND as far from Taiwan and involving only coastal artillery units; Liaoning CSG conducted western Pacific drills ~14 Oct; no large-scale encirclement exercise has occurred in 2026 to date.
taiwan_tension.rationale: Persistent median-line crossings and assertive naval presence satisfy Rubric 1 (assertive patrols/large-scale drills). No kinetic clash, blockade, or full mobilization has occurred, ruling out Rubric 2; and the daily count (3 sorties, 1 crossing) is below the mid-October spike, confirming no new escalation since Oct 19.

export_controls.fact: On 16 October 2026, MOFCOM and MOST issued Joint Announcement No. 48 of 2026 proposing export controls on 40 technologies (AI, chips, solar, biomedicine) with a temporary registration requirement effective immediately (sources: tech-insider.org, ainvesting.org, superkalam.com citing AP/Reuters, dated Oct 16-17 2026). Prior Chinese countermeasures remain in force: June 2026 dual-use supply bans on 10 US companies, July 2026 addition of Dutch/Rheinmetall entities to China's Export Control List, and ongoing rare-earth controls targeting ASML's EUV supply chain. On the US/allied side, the MATCH Act (targeting DUV/ASML China sales) passed House Foreign Affairs Committee 36-8 on April 22, 2026 and remains actively advancing; EU/NL DUV immersion lithography controls are in force.
export_controls.rationale: Both the US/allied side (MATCH Act advancing, existing DUV and metrology controls in force) and the Chinese side (Oct 16 Announcement No. 48 with immediate registration effect, plus prior entity-list additions and supply bans) have enacted or are enacting active measures within the trailing 3 months, satisfying rubric level 2 (RETALIATION: target country enacts countermeasures). No de-escalation signal is found in price or volume data.

dissent.view: China's Oct 16 proposal is not yet final law — it is a draft for public comment, so some analysts may rate it as level 1 (tightening only from allied side) pending Chinese rule finalization; however, the immediately operative temporary registration requirement is a binding interim measure.

fab_concentration.fact: TSMC Q3 2026 earnings call (Oct 15 2026, SEC Form 6-K): N3 capacity ~180,000 wpm and N2 ramping toward ~100,000 wpm — all in Taiwan. Arizona Fab 21 Phase 2 (N3): equipment installation underway Q3 2026, 'production set to start in the third quarter of 2027' (Evertiq, Oct 19 2026). Japan JASM Fab 2 (3nm): HVM 2028. Zero <=3nm wafers produced outside Taiwan as of today.
fab_concentration.rationale: All operational <=3nm capacity (~260,000+ wpm combined N2+N3) is exclusively in Taiwan; Arizona Fab 21 Phase 2 is in equipment-installation phase with no wafer output until H2 2027 and Japan 3nm not until 2028. This places the current share of <=3nm capacity outside Taiwan at 0%, firmly within the EXTREME (<10%, no operational overseas leading-edge fab) rubric band.

hormuz_redsea_status.fact: IMF PortWatch recorded 4 commercial transits through the Strait of Hormuz on October 18 2026, against a pre-crisis baseline of ~85/day (~4.7% of baseline); Brent at ~$115-117/bbl; UKMTO reported a tanker struck by projectile on October 22; IRGC claims two supertankers struck mines in the strait (unconfirmed, Oct 24-25); Reuters reports ship attacks in Hormuz hit record high in October (straits.live briefs, Oct 24-26 2026, sourcing IMF PortWatch).
hormuz_redsea_status.rationale: At ~4.7% of baseline the Strait of Hormuz is far below the 25% threshold for CLOSED (rating 2); Bab el-Mandeb at ~26/day (~37% of baseline, week ending Oct 18) rates CONTESTED (1) with ongoing Houthi attacks on Saudi-linked shipping. The rubric requires rating the worse of the two chokepoints, so Hormuz at 2 governs.

dissent.view: Bab el-Mandeb transits grew ~4% in September per Lloyd's List (Oct 15 brief) and preliminary weekly avg was ~280 total vessels in late September/early October per Lloyd's List Oct 1 brief, suggesting the Red Sea leg is recovering; but IMF PortWatch AIS data for week ending Oct 18 shows only 26/day, consistent with a sharp post-Houthi-offensive dip, and the Hormuz figure is unchanged.

cable_incidents.fact: Reuters (Oct 23-25, 2026), citing two senior Iranian security officials, reported Iran has drawn up detailed plans to attack undersea communications cables in the Persian Gulf if US-Israeli strikes resume, with IRGC official Yadollah Javani publicly warning seven major cables beneath the Strait of Hormuz are 'legitimate targets'; no cable cut has been confirmed and TeleGeography confirms no Hormuz connectivity loss.
cable_incidents.rationale: Active, named-official, Reuters-confirmed threats against specific Hormuz cables (AAE-1 singled out by IRGC) satisfy rubric level 1 ('credible official threats'); no cable is severed or unrepaired today, and no price/connectivity signal supports escalation to level 2.

treasury_clearing_rollout.fact: SIFMA/DTCC/BNY/Broadridge pulse survey (Sept 22, 2026, n=340): 86% of respondents at least somewhat confident of meeting the overall mandate; 13% 'not confident' for cash, 16% for repo; 88% of delayed programs cite legal/contract negotiation; 45% still need more regulatory clarity; 51% have no formal contingency plan; 59% of project activity will complete after the cash deadline. SEC Commissioner Uyeda (Sept 22, 2026 US Treasury Market Conference): 'the SEC does not currently intend to extend these deadlines.'
treasury_clearing_rollout.rationale: 86% confidence clears the rubric's <60% threshold, and no deadline extension or major operational failure has occurred, ruling out a '2'. However, persistent legal/documentation backlogs (88% of delayed firms cite contract negotiation), 13% cash non-confidence with ~65 days to deadline, 45% needing regulatory clarity, and 51% lacking contingency plans sustain a '1 = FRICTION' reading.

oat_bund.fact: As of 26 October 2026 market close, the 10Y OAT-Bund spread tightened to 154 basis points (OAT 4.9016%, Bund 3.3589%), per Boursorama citing Reuters tickers FR10YT=RR and DE10YT=RR at 18:27 CET; intraday sources (Newsquawk ~158 bps, FXStreet ~163 bps) corroborate the directional tightening from the 23 Oct close of 171.8 bps (ideal-investisseur.fr / Banque de France & Bundesbank) and the 22 Oct peak of 174.6-176 bps.
oat_bund.rationale: The rubric requires the latest 10Y OAT minus Bund spread in percentage points from the past 7 days; 154 bps = 1.54 pp, sourced from same-day Reuters-tickered data via Boursorama (26 Oct 2026), superseding the prior reading of 1.423 (19 Oct 2026). The spread widened sharply post-19 Oct (peak ~175 bps on 22-23 Oct) then partially tightened after Moody's held France at Aa3 on 24 Oct; the new load-bearing fact is materially different from the prior week's 142.3 bps.
oat_bund.change_reason: new_event: OAT-Bund spread surged ~30 bps in the week of 20-23 Oct 2026 (reaching 174.6 bps on 22 Oct, a 2011 eurozone-crisis high) driven by fiscal fears and political unrest, then partially retraced to ~154 bps on 26 Oct after Moody's held France's Aa3 rating unchanged (24 Oct 2026). Net change from prior reading: +11.7 bps.

dissent.view: FXStreet (26 Oct 2026 morning) cited OAT-Bund spread at ~163 bps, with OAT at 4.97%; Newsquawk (26 Oct morning) cited ~158 bps low vs Friday peak of 176 bps — both are earlier intraday readings that preceded the 154 bps end-of-day level
Cbonds data showed 168.4 bps on 23 Oct 2026 (vs ideal-investisseur.fr's 171.8 bps on the same date) — minor source discrepancy on the 23 Oct close
